title: Session checkpoint handoff and adaptive circuit-shedding for graceful regional switchover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a coordinated, session-aware regional switchover technique for the hosted API gateway that minimizes user-visible stream interruptions. The approach uses lightweight per-connection checkpoints (commit-delete leases), a short soft-lease TTL exchange between gateways, and an adaptive per-connection circuit-shedding heuristic to protect regional capacity while preserving resumability for in-flight streaming sessions. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with the edge gateway, and an incremental rollout plan tied to SLO guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: New checkpoint handshake is implemented in gateway proxy and runtime clients; checkpoints are stored in the existing fast KV with <= 5ms median write latency
During a controlled regional drain, >= 95% of streaming sessions resume from checkpoint with no more than one user-visible reconnect
Failover-triggered load shedding keeps 99th-percentile tail latency for control-plane ACKs below 300ms under 2x baseline traffic
Circuit-shedding decisions are logged and surfaced in Console with per-route drop counts and reason codes
Automated canary release and rollback for the feature completes without exceeding SLO error budget for the canary group
tasks: Design protocol: lease handshake format, checkpoint fields (seq id, partial KV pointers, last-token-offset)
Implement checkpoint write/read API in gateway proxy (C++), with idempotent writes and expiry semantics
Extend runtime client to accept resume token and attempt checkpoint resume before full session restart
Add adaptive circuit-shedding module: metrics ingestion (queue depth, token backlog, p50/p95 latency) -> shedding decision
Integrate shedder metrics with Console and create telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds
Create canary pipeline: 0.5%, 2%, 10% increments with automated SLO checks and rollback hooks
Run chaos experiments simulating region partition and capacity spikes; document learnings
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization, idempotency, and TTL expiry
Stress test: synthetic streaming workload with checkpointing enabled across two regions; measure resume success rate
Fault injection: broker acks delayed and KV writes fail transiently; verify client fallback behavior and circuit tripping
Soak test: 24h at 1.5x normal traffic during canary to watch for regressions in cost or latency
A/B test comparing current soft-drain method vs checkpoint-handoff under identical traffic profiles
rollout_plan: Feature flagged: default off for all customers
Phase 1 (internal): enable for infra-only tenants and internal traffic for 1 week
Phase 2 (canary): 0.5% production traffic for 48h. Run SLO checks; if OK, increase to 2% for 72h
Phase 3 (wider): 10% production traffic for 4 days with active monitoring and on-call playbook ready
Phase 4 (enable): Gradual ramp to 100% across regions, with per-region thresholds and automated rollback if shedder events exceed limits
Finalize: mark runtime clients that support resume as GA and publish SDK upgrade notes
monitoring_signals: Resume success rate (sessions resumed / sessions with checkpoint) - target >= 95%
Per-route shed rate and shed reason distribution
Client-side reconnects per session (spikes indicate regressions)
Regional capacity headroom (GPU/queue metrics) and circuit open fraction
SLO burn: errors and latency for canary cohort compared to baseline
notes: This design intentionally favors resumability for long-lived streaming sessions (video-to-text, multi-turn chat) over a small increase in control-plane complexity.
We selected a soft-lease TTL of 10s for initial experiments to balance quick failover with resume opportunities; TTL may be tuned by route.
Fallback: if checkpoint read fails during resume, client will fall back to full session restart and emit a resumability failure metric
Security: checkpoints contain opaque byte offsets and last-stable-token hashes only; no plaintext user data is stored
Operational playbook will include steps to forcibly drain checkpoints from KV in case of datastore corruption
